Mood: neutral - woke up feeling a bit restless, maybe too much screen time last night.

Tonight was quiet. I cooked pasta with garlic and olive oil, added some spinach I had left. The kitchen smelled nice. I took my time, no rush. After dinner, I tidied up a corner of the living room, just moved some books around. It felt good to organize. I left my phone in the bedroom, no notifications, just silence. I sat on the couch for a while, looking out the window. The street was calm, just a few cars. I enjoyed the stillness. Nothing happened, and that was nice. Just a good ordinary evening.

So I moved my workspace to the coffee shop down the street and shifted my hours to start later in the day, dropped that early morning meeting I dreaded. I thought it would feel liberating, like I’d finally have the freedom to work when I’m most productive, but honestly, it’s been a mixed bag. The first few days were great, I felt energized and excited, but then I started to miss the structure of my old routine, like I’m not sure when to take breaks and I end up working way too long without realizing it. It’s only been a week, so I know I need to give it more time, but I’m surprised how much I miss that early morning quiet time. I’ll keep an eye on my productivity and mood over the next few weeks to see if this really works for me or if I need to adjust again.

finish that feature for the app, call mom, laundry, update resume, send that email to the client, buy groceries, research new tech stack, fix the bug in the code, plan weekend trip, clean the kitchen, remember to water the plants, get a haircut, prep for the meeting, organize files, schedule dentist appointment, need to follow up on that project, read that book on productivity, oh and don’t forget to check in with the team, wow this is a lot, maybe just writing it down helps, feels lighter already but where to even start...
Finally closed the tax return task that had been hanging around for about 6 months. Moved it from list to list way too many times (never again).

I just hit my 10th project completion, and this time I did it all on my own. It took a lot of late nights and pushing through self-doubt, but I’m proud of how far I've come. This is a big deal for me, feeling like I can handle things solo now.

It's interesting to reflect on how I used to dread debugging code, it felt like pulling teeth, hours spent wrestling with errors that seemed impossible to crack. I remember sitting for days on a single issue, feeling so overwhelmed. But now, I just fixed a bug in a couple of minutes without even breaking a sweat. It’s like my brain has rewired itself to handle these challenges more efficiently. I hardly even noticed the change until now, but debugging has become just another part of the process, a task that feels almost effortless. Progress is subtle but real.
Walked 1.5 miles today, which is more than I usually do. Cooked a healthy dinner instead of ordering takeout again. Not huge, but it feels good to take these little steps!

Today, my colleague said, 'You really nailed that project, your attention to detail made a huge difference.' It felt really good to hear that, kind of awkward to write it down but I know I need to keep this for later. I often forget these little wins and they really help boost my confidence. So saving it here to remind myself that I’m doing well sometimes, even when I doubt it. Need to remember to celebrate these moments more.
